The Esquipulas Peace Agreement was signed by the presidents of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica on 7 August 1987 in Guatemala City. It set out a plan to end the civil wars of Central America.

The plan was drawn up by President Óscar Arias of Costa Rica, who won the Nobel Peace Prize for it that year. It called for ceasefires, amnesties, an end to foreign help for rebels, and free elections. It was named after Esquipulas in Guatemala, where the presidents had first met in 1986.

The United States, which backed the Contras, was sceptical. But the process led to elections in Nicaragua in 1990, the Chapultepec accords in El Salvador in 1992 and peace in Guatemala in 1996.
sum: The Esquipulas Peace Agreement was signed by the presidents of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica on 7 August 1987 in Guatemala City. It set out a plan to end the civil wars of Central America.
